title: Cairo Desk – Saturday 17 October 2026
desc: Sisi asks parliament for authority to defend Saudi Arabia if asked; Sisi says he will leave office in 2030 and sources differ; prison visits by the National Council for Human Rights versus reports of prison protests; Matsda2sh journalists' detention renewed; Egypt Forum economic planning, bread and the pound; social security programme; Giza school placements; Briefly: Palestinian meeting in Cairo and gold-mining crackdown; And finally: the Haram video case. Sources: Al-Dostour, Al-Shorouk, Mada Masr (summaries only); Al-Ahram and Al-Masry Al-Youm unreachable.

title: Cairo Desk – Sunday 18 October 2026
desc: Running order: Sisi says his term ends in 2030 and the constitution will not be touched, with party reactions and the debate on who may run; Parliament asked to prepare an emergency session on defending Saudi Arabia; the Egypt Forum opens 19 October; Banque du Caire share sale heavily oversubscribed; Briefly: Safaga sailors, al-Maris police shooting, Alexandria death sentences, Central Bank fake job warning; And finally: the seven-thousand-year claim. Sources: Al-Dostor, Al-Shorouk, Enterprise. Al-Ahram, Mada Masr and Al-Masry Al-Youm could not be reached.

title: Cairo Desk – Monday 19 October 2026
desc: Parliament prepares a vote authorising Egyptian forces to defend Saudi Arabia; Sisi says his term ends in 2030 and a candidate-training plan sparks a constitutional debate; governors lobby MPs over the new local administration law; the Wafd Party heads for internal elections; Brotherhood financial committees trial adjourned; briefly, Mostaqbal Watan in Matrouh and a Senate request on international education. Sources: Al-Shorouk and Al-Dostor; Al-Ahram, Al-Masry Al-Youm and Mada Masr could not be reached.

title: Cairo Desk – Tuesday 20 October 2026
desc: Running order: Sisi opens the six-day Egypt Forum 2026 in the New Capital; the cabinet's rumour-checking platform; reported remarks on preparing cadres to take over the presidency after 2030; a possible parliamentary authorisation on defending Saudi Arabia; calls for local council elections; building-violations reconciliation deadline extended to May 2027; briefly, MPs' reactions, hospital equipment, school attendance figures, youth centres; and finally Bassem Youssef at the forum. Sources reached: Dostor and Shorouk. Ahram, Mada Masr and Al-Masry Al-Youm could not be reached.
